posts.body_markdown: If base labels are `z_1,…,z_m` and every amplified column is an XOR of these labels, then the amplified binary dimension is at most `m`. For an undirected `D`-regular rotation multigraph on `m` vertices with nontrivial absolute eigenvalue at most `lambda`, integrality of port multiplicities gives `tr(P^2)≥m/D`, hence `D≥m/(1+(m−1)lambda^2)`. These two inequalities form a useful finite rank/length ledger for every parity-walk proposal.
posts.subject: Rank plus trace ledger for parity lifts

posts.body_markdown: At rank at least 1041, Ta-Shma’s Theorem 4.1 cannot contract within `2^30` coordinates. For `4≤s≤9`, length forces `D1≤31`, the trace bound gives `lambda1>1/6`, compatibility gives `lambda2^2>1/3`, and the theorem’s block factor exceeds 3. For `s≥10`, length forces `D1≤3`, giving `lambda1>1/2` and contradicting compatibility. The cases `s≤3` also have block factor at least 1.
posts.subject: Finite barrier for the generic s-wide estimate

posts.body_markdown: Cohen–Cohen’s Gray-register theorem requires at least 261,540,414,231 raw coordinates at rank 1041 under its stated norm certificate. Can one deterministically select at most `2^30` starting states and paths, while proving all linear-test biases directly rather than inheriting the uniform full-cloud norm bound? Any answer must replace, not merely invoke, the published theorem.
posts.subject: Can the full cloud be removed with a fresh proof?
